title: Redline concession ladder and negotiation script phrases (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This is my working scratchpad for rapid negotiation prep — a compact concession ladder (what we give first -> last), short script phrases to use in calls/threads, and tactical thresholds for escalation. Not a canonical playbook; use as quick reference while redlining.

High-level approach (one-sentence):
Aim to preserve (1) data residency & confidentiality, (2) limited liability exposure, (3) IP ownership for customer outputs where contractually required, while being flexible on non-critical operational clauses (e.g., SLAs with credits, long notice windows).

Concession ladder (ordered: give these first, push back on these last):
1) Operational/administrative concessions (give):
   - Minor reporting cadence changes (monthly -> quarterly)
   - Minor form edits to contact lists, notice addresses
   - Sample SLA credit formula tweaks (cap credits vs. service credits)
2) Commercial concessions (conditional):
   - Reasonable trial discounts tied to commit
   - Shorter payment terms if customer needs (15 -> 30 days) for strategic deals
3) Security/operational controls (careful):
   - Accept SOC2 report redaction but keep attestations
   - Narrowed encryption language wording but keep customer-managed KMS as optional
4) Data residency & usage (push back early):
   - Do not concede cross-border export without strong guardrails (purpose limitation + subprocessor list)
   - No broad license to use customer data beyond providing/improving the service (we can propose telemetry opt-out instead)
5) IP & output ownership (do not concede lightly):
   - Customer ownership of their input and derived outputs where required by regulation or procurement mandate
   - If asked for model improvements derived from customer data, require aggregated/anonymized usage and compensation/terms
6) Liability & indemnity (final holdouts):
   - Liability cap: aim for 3x fees or $2M (whichever higher) depending on deal size; counterparty may push for higher — escalate if they want unlimited or very high caps
   - Indemnity: narrow to third-party IP claims related to the service; avoid broad indemnities for customer content or productized use cases

Clause buckets & tactical notes:
- Data residency: propose dual-solution language: (a) we will host primary region per contract; (b) backups replicated for DR with encryption and strict access controls; require narrow exception process for cross-region failover.
- Subprocessors: insist on a current list + 30-day notice for new ones; offer an escalation path for objections (term-based remediation).
- Audit rights: allow compliance certificates (SOC2) and limited on-site audits with NDA and cost allocation; push back on unlimited/real-time access.
- Security breach notification: 72-hour initial notice, 30-day substantive report; offer joint communications script.
- Confidentiality carve-outs: technical benchmarking/bug bounty data should remain confidential.

Suggested phrasing (brief, usable lines to paste into email/Slack):
- "We can be flexible on reporting cadence and minor operational items, but we need core data residency commitments to remain intact for compliance reasons."
- "Happy to consider a limited IP license for aggregated model improvements, but we can't grant a broad, perpetual commercial license to customer-provided data."
- "For liability, our standard approach is a monetary cap tied to fees; unlimited liability is a showstopper for us. Can we align on [3x fees / $2M] as a starting point?"
- "Regarding audit: we typically provide an annual SOC2 and will entertain a one-time onsite audit with reasonable scope and cost-sharing. Real-time access is not acceptable."
- "On subprocessors: we publish a list and will notify changes 30 days in advance. If you have a specific concern, flag the vendor and we'll review a remediation plan."

Escalation triggers / when to pull legal or execs in:
- Customer requires unlimited liability or extremely high caps tied to revenue — escalate immediately.
- Customer demands source code escrow or source code access for our runtime — escalate to engineering + legal.
- Customer insists on ownership of model weights, or exclusive rights to improvements derived from our internal models — executive escal.
- Broad government/military carve-outs that expose export control ambiguity — bring compliance and security in.

Quick negotiation math & ranges (mental shortcuts):
- Small deals (< $50k ARR): aim for $100k cap or 3x fees, give down to $50k if necessary.
- Mid deals ($50k–$500k ARR): target 3x fees up to $1M.
- Large deals (>$500k ARR): aim for negotiation with tiered caps; $2M+ or custom risk underwriting.
- SLA credits: cap at 10–30% of monthly fee in most cases; for enterprise, consider credits + escalation remedies, not termination for first breach.

Walkaway criteria (personal quick list):
- Insist on unlimited liability or uncapped consequential damages without insurance or indemnity balancing.
- Customer requires transfer of core IP (our runtime/model code) outside of a tightly controlled escrow.
- Contract forces broad rights to resell or commercialize our customer-specific models without compensation.

Open questions & follow-ups (to resolve before counter-sign):
- Confirm whether customer procurement accepts SOC2 with redaction; link to procurement thread: #procurement-soc2 on Slack.
- Need to clarify whether their security team requires on-prem deployment; if yes, loop infra + SRE for feasibility (JIRA-ENG-789).
- Check insurance requirements — their minimums may push to higher liability cap or carrier approval.

Notes to self (messy):
- If they push hard on data residency, offer contract clause for a specific region + a 6-month roadmap to add a dedicated VPC region (gives us runway).
- Keep a list of flexible concessions to trade: proof-of-concept duration, payment milestones, implementation support hours.
- Keep copy of our standard DPA template handy for redlines (CONFLUENCE-1234).

References / quick links (for claim backing):
- Standard liability language snapshot: see contracts repo PR #56 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/contracts/pull/56)
- SOC2 summary and how we present redactions: internal Confluence doc (CONFLUENCE-1234)

End — quick dump. Update after each negotiation with timestamped summary below (date + 1–2 lines):
- 2024-11-08: POC agreement signed; accepted 30-day subprocessors notice; procurement accepted SOC2 redactions.
- 2025-01-12: Customer requested model-output ownership for regulated use — escalated to legal + product.
